title: Count the Vowels
description:
Given a string `s`, return how many vowels it contains. The vowels are `a`, `e`, `i`, `o` and `u`, in both lowercase and uppercase.

Example: for `s = "hello"` return `2` (`e` and `o`).
hints: Concept: you can look at each character with `s.charAt(i)`. To check whether a character is a vowel, compare it against each vowel, or check whether `"aeiouAEIOU"` contains it.
Approach: keep a counter starting at 0. Visit every character, and add 1 to the counter whenever the character is a vowel.

workedExample.title: Count the Digits
workedExample.description: Return how many characters in `s` are digits (`0` to `9`).
workedExample.explanation:
This is the counting pattern again: one counter, one loop, one condition.

The condition is the only part that changes between problems. Here it checks for a digit. For your problem it needs to check for a vowel.

walkthrough.note: 'h' is not a vowel. count stays 0.
'o' is a vowel! count becomes 2. Return 2.

mistakes.hint: Uppercase vowels count too. Check for "AEIOU" as well as "aeiou".
